stem: Two cultivars are staged close together with similar-looking cut branches. What control is strongest?
choices: Rely on visual branch differences to keep the cultivars separate during movement.
Remove labels once material is in the same receiving room because room location becomes the new identity.
Combine the branches temporarily and separate them by appearance before final receiving.
Maintain verified lot/container labels and physical separation throughout movement and receiving so similar material cannot be mixed.
rationale: Similar-looking cut material is especially vulnerable to identity mix-ups. The strongest control is to preserve verified labels and physical separation from source through receiving. Visual recognition is not a substitute for controlled identity, and temporary mixing can break traceability even if staff believe they can separate the material later.
